title: Grid BFS: many sources
summary: Steps from every open cell to its nearest exit, or -1 for walls and unreachable cells. Seed every exit at distance 0, then expand in four directions; a cell's first visit is final. O(rows × cols).
code: # All exits start in the queue, so a cell's first visit gives its nearest exit.
nr, nc = r + dr, c + dc
inside = 0 <= nr < rows and 0 <= nc < cols
if inside and grid[nr][nc] != '#' and distance[nr][nc] == -1:
triggers: distance to the nearest of many sources on a grid
something spreads one cell per step from several starting cells at once
prompts: A warehouse floor plan marks shelves, open aisles and loading docks. For each open spot, how many steps is it to the closest dock?
A fire starts in several rooms of a floor plan at once and spreads to neighbouring rooms each minute, never through walls. When does each room catch fire?
invariant: The queue holds cells in nondecreasing distance, starting with every exit at 0, so the first distance written to a cell is its shortest.
mantra: Seed every source, then expand one ring at a time.
pitfalls: Seed all sources before the loop; one BFS per source multiplies the work by the number of sources.
Check bounds before indexing: 0 <= nr < rows and 0 <= nc < cols.
Mark a cell when you enqueue it, as in graph BFS.

anchors.name: Rotting Oranges
anchors.trick: Seed every rotten orange; the answer is the largest distance, or -1 if a fresh orange is never reached.

anchors.name: 01 Matrix
anchors.trick: Seed every 0 cell; each 1 gets its distance to the nearest 0.

anchors.name: Walls and Gates
anchors.trick: Exactly this, with gates as exits.

mutations.explanation: Seeds only the first exit. The others count as open cells, so every distance is measured from that one exit.
